key.name: manual-latitude
key.summary: Latitude for sunrise/sunset calculation.
key.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (e.g., 37.7749 for San Francisco). North is positive, south is negative. Range: -90 to 90. Can be set manually or via the Auto-Detect button.

key.name: manual-longitude
key.summary: Longitude for sunrise/sunset calculation.
key.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (e.g., -122.4194 for San Francisco). East is positive, west is negative. Range: -180 to 180. Can be set manually or via the Auto-Detect button.

key.name: location-name
key.summary: Human-readable location name
key.description: Display name for the configured location (e.g., "San Francisco, California, USA"). Set automatically when using Auto-Detect, or can be left empty for manual coordinates.

key.name: control-brightness
key.summary: Control screen brightness gradually throughout the day.

key.name: last-brightness-update
key.summary: Timestamp (in milliseconds) of the last brightness update.

key.name: last-session-id
key.summary: Session ID from last enable() call to distinguish login from unlock.

key.name: gradual-brightness-decrease-enabled
key.summary: Enable gradual brightness decrease before dark mode.

key.name: gradual-brightness-decrease-duration
key.summary: Duration in seconds to gradually decrease brightness before dark mode trigger (default: 2 hours).

key.name: gradual-brightness-increase-enabled
key.summary: Enable gradual brightness increase before light mode.

key.name: gradual-brightness-increase-duration
key.summary: Duration in seconds to gradually increase brightness before light mode trigger (default: 2 hours).

key.name: light-theme
key.summary: The GTK theme to use during the day.

key.name: dark-theme
key.summary: The GTK theme to use at night.

key.name: true-light-mode
key.summary: Enable True Light Mode - makes the top bar/shell light in addition to GTK apps.
key.description: When enabled, switches the system color-scheme preference to make the GNOME Shell top bar light. When disabled, only GTK themes are switched while keeping the shell/top bar dark. Note: This option only affects systems using stock GNOME (like Fedora). Ubuntu keeps the top bar dark by default regardless of this setting.

key.name: night-light-mode
key.summary: Night Light control mode ('disabled', 'sync-with-theme', or 'custom-schedule').

key.name: night-light-start-time
key.summary: Time to enable Night Light (HH:MM) when using custom schedule.

key.name: night-light-end-time
key.summary: Time to disable Night Light (HH:MM) when using custom schedule.

key.name: show-notifications
key.summary: Show notifications when the theme is switched automatically.

key.name: light-mode-trigger
key.summary: What time to use for switching to light mode ('first-light', 'dawn', 'sunrise', 'solar-noon', or 'custom').
key.description: Solar event triggers require coordinates to be set. If coordinates are empty, falls back to custom time. - first-light: Astronomical dawn (sun 18 degrees below horizon) - dawn: Civil dawn (sun 6 degrees below horizon) - sunrise: Sun crosses the horizon - solar-noon: Sun at highest point - custom: Use the custom-light-time setting

key.name: dark-mode-trigger
key.summary: What time to use for switching to dark mode ('solar-noon', 'golden-hour', 'sunset', 'dusk', 'last-light', or 'custom').
key.description: Solar event triggers require coordinates to be set. If coordinates are empty, falls back to custom time. - solar-noon: Sun at highest point - golden-hour: Sun 6 degrees above horizon (warm light for photography) - sunset: Sun crosses the horizon - dusk: Civil dusk (sun 6 degrees below horizon) - last-light: Astronomical dusk (sun 18 degrees below horizon) - custom: Use the custom-dark-time setting

key.name: custom-light-time
key.summary: The custom time (HH:MM) to switch to light mode if light-mode-trigger is 'custom' or no coordinates are set.

key.name: custom-dark-time
key.summary: The custom time (HH:MM) to switch to dark mode if dark-mode-trigger is 'custom' or no coordinates are set.

key.name: monitors
key.summary: JSON array of all monitor configurations (built-in and external)
key.description: Stores configuration for all monitors including: - Built-in display (via brightnessctl) - External monitors (via ddcutil with DDC/CI protocol) Each monitor includes: - Monitor identification (type, manufacturer, model, serial number) - Display number and I2C bus (for external monitors) - Light and dark mode brightness values - Gradual transition durations (increase/decrease) - Enabled/disabled state - Last seen timestamp

key.name: monitors-last-detection
key.summary: Unix timestamp (milliseconds) of last monitor detection
key.description: Used to show "last detected" time in the UI

key.name: data-version
key.summary: Data structure version for migrations
key.description: Version of the data structure format. Used to determine which migrations to run. Version history: - 0: Original published version with light-brightness/dark-brightness keys, API-based location detection and solar calculations (pre-v6) - 1: Current version with monitors array (built-in + external monitors), local solar calculations, removed API dependencies (v6+) Future versions will be numbered 2, 3, etc.

key.name: migration-notification-pending
key.summary: Pending migration notification type
key.description: Set by MigrationManager after a migration completes. The ExtensionController reads this on startup to show a one-time notification, then clears it. Values: '' (none), 'v0-to-v1' (location detection changed)

key.name: manual-mode-active
key.summary: Manual override mode active
key.description: When true, the user has explicitly chosen a theme via the Manual Override section in the prefs Status tab. The auto schedule and time-based brightness loop are paused until the user clicks Reset. Persisted so the override survives extension reloads (screen lock, suspend/resume, GNOME Shell reload).

key.name: manual-mode-is-dark
key.summary: Manual override chosen mode
key.description: When manual-mode-active is true, records whether the user chose dark (true) or light (false). Used to re-apply the user's choice after extension reload and on screen-unlock or monitor-hotplug events.

key.name: debug-logging
key.summary: Enable debug logging
key.description: When enabled, the extension writes verbose diagnostic messages to the system journal. Off by default to keep the journal quiet.
